B2.protocol: 10 fixed lifecycle/admission cases, 31 generation points, 620 recorded windows. Two independent warmups then seven uninstrumented timing and three allocator repetitions. Four retained generations plus initial graph; no case selection or retries.
B2.read_only: Snapshot/fork-insert median query-window gains coexist with deeper clone allocations and retained memory. Some timing ranges overlap; snapshot6/fork-insert6 have large outliers, so no uniform latency claim.
B2.discarded_copy: First fork-tombstone with six warmed projections copies all six, invalidates them after actual deletion, then materializes one new requested projection. Later generations retain only the requested one.
B2.allocation_parity: Every in-place-insert generation has identical main/candidate requested allocation bytes despite pre-existing tombstones.
B2.heap_limits: Reported store overlay heap excludes shared base and sums initial +retained generations; heap_bytes omits boxed Overlay metadata and estimates hash-table capacity. Requested-live counters separately include fixed allocation sizes. Process RSS is cumulative from setup and cannot isolate query heap.

B3.invariant: Overlay and TripleStore.overlay are private. Full-workspace mutation inventory finds only two production tombstone mutators, both in TripleStore.apply_delta; test-only direct extends are explicitly identified.
B3.replacement: from_triples/from_triples_compressed/open construct no overlay. Graph compaction merges live triples and replaces the store. clear-default either uses apply_delta or replaces the store. WAL replay/redo use apply_delta_mem/apply_delta. persist_swap adopts a freshly reopened graph; vacuum constructs a fresh re-interned graph then swaps. These routes do not transplant stale projections into a different base or dictionary. into_compressed scans the merged live view and constructs a new compressed TripleStore with no overlay; save/save_compressed fold through store persistence and recursively save named graphs.
B3.limits: Source verification for mmap/WAL/compaction/restore; no new durable-store or crash-injection execution in this scoped revision.

N1_N2: Runtime docs now state up to BUILT.len() vectors of twelve-byte rows plus slack, in addition to deletion hash set, and synchronized cold first-reader sorting. Derived Clone deep-copies initialized vectors unchanged.
N3: Real three-pattern SELECT validates all four expected bindings; separate oracle has exactly 1179648 added projection bytes (3*32768*12). Two cold concurrent readers return correct rows; allocator live growth is one 393216-byte vector, not two. Individual reader durations are recorded, not tail percentiles.
limitations: Local Apple M1 diagnostic only; no canonical performance claim or broad parameter sweep.
No service publication, retained server snapshots, durable I/O, allocator metadata, mapped/stack memory, or end-to-end tail latency measured.
Full workspace, wasm, W3C, Miri and canonical ratchets remain outside this authorized scoped run.

amortization.interpretation: Saved medians imply approximately 7 total same-shape reads per true-tombstone generation or 5 multi-pattern reads to repay cold work, under the explicit no-intervening-change/linear-cost assumptions. This is algebra, not a measured admission threshold and does not remove retained memory or cold tail cost.
